methodology.throughput: Precomputed deterministic ANSI, warmed 32 updates; repeated blocks of 32, GPU-fenced every block. DOM forces layout and has no GPU-completion fence. Grid recorded in config. Legacy complex/churn/append/showcase/pipes use the existing fixed-frame comparison harness. Synchronous core throughput is distinct from worker SDK latency.
methodology.correctness: Fixed-count replay text hashes compared with upstream DOM; WebGL viewport must match drawing-buffer dimensions. Initial real pixels checked for every renderer/DPR. Unicode11 enabled on xterm workflow cases; native Unicode glyph coverage is not certified by a text-state match.
methodology.latency: Real Playwright keyboard events; key→onData, echo parse acknowledgement, public onRender notification, then next rAF opportunity. Native onRender is opt-in; notification observes submission, not GPU completion or actual display scanout. Output flood offers ~64KiB every 16ms with a 2MiB queue cap; achieved rates retained.
methodology.memory: Eight public SDK terminals, 80x24 each, bounded 10000-line histories. Main-page JS heap (excluding native worker heaps and most GPU/Wasm allocations) and isolated Chrome process RSS sampled before/load/after disposal; RSS sums can double-count shared mappings. These are bounded-run observations, not proof of leak absence.
methodology.cpu: Isolated Chrome process CPU-time deltas / elapsed wall time. 100% means one busy logical CPU; also divided by logical CPU count for machine capacity. Process-set changes invalidate this estimate.
methodology.gpu: Device-wide Apple GPU driver utilization during sustained runs. Includes other apps and has an undocumented averaging window; cannot be attributed to this terminal process.
methodology.timing: Headless Chrome with real GPU; no other benchmark runs concurrently. Browser performance.now precision applies. Desktop apps and device thermals are not controlled.
